label: Research pool 23 Oct: university spin-outs and deep tech

payload.writeUp: Claude Code research, 23 Oct 2026: UK university spin-outs and deep-tech companies raising now, mainly from SETsquared's Investment Futures 2026 (investor event, 24 Nov 2026, CodeNode London; every presenting company must be actively raising £250k–£5m) and its Medtech Spotlight (29 Sep 2026). The open round and its size are SETsquared's statement, not the company's; the route is registering for the event and booking founder meetings, or a founder intro. No page read states SEIS/EIS or a valuation.

candidate.name: Xerode
candidate.teaser: University of Sheffield spin-out printing battery electrodes dry, without solvents; raising £2m.
candidate.description: Xerode is a University of Sheffield spin-out (incorporated April 2026, per the university) developing a solvent-free, dry digital printing process for battery electrodes, aimed at cutting the cost, energy use and factory footprint of electrode coating. The founding team are Sheffield academics: CEO Dr Yufeng Lai, CSO Prof Rachel Smith and CTO Dr Denis Cumming, with John Walker as Executive Chair. The company claims 32% CapEx, 22% OpEx and 43% energy savings; these are company claims, not independently verified. SETsquared lists its ask as £2m at Investment Futures 2026. Main risks: very early (months-old company), hardware scale-up, and competition from established dry-electrode efforts.

candidate.teaser: Cardiff-based spin-out with a chemotaxis-based platform to make tumour-targeting cell therapies; asking £1m.
candidate.description: CoED Biosciences is developing its Column of Expansion and Differentiation (CoED) platform, which uses natural chemotaxis rather than mechanical sorting to manufacture tumour-hunting cell therapies for solid tumours. The founders say the technology was spun out of academic labs at Queen Mary University of London and the University of Bristol and incorporated through the Science Creates Accelerator; it is now headquartered at Cardiff Medicentre. Co-founders are Dr David Coe (CEO/CSO) and Dr Saeed Fathi (CTO). SETsquared lists a £1m ask. Risks: long biotech timelines, capital intensity beyond seed, and no disclosed partners or revenue.
